\section{Introduction}

An \emph{impossible figure} is a drawing the visual system reads as a solid
object for which no consistent solid exists. The celebrated examples are the
\textbf{Penrose triangle} (three beams forming a loop, each apparently receding)
and the \textbf{Escher staircase} (a closed flight of stairs on which every step
rises). Roger Penrose (\emph{On the cohomology of impossible figures}, 1992)
observed that the impossibility is not a local defect: every small region depicts
a realizable fragment, and the contradiction only manifests around the whole
loop.

We formalize this insight completely and elementarily. The mathematical content
is the first cohomology of a circle with abelian coefficients, but we require no
prior cohomology: the theory reduces to the fact that a sum around a cycle
telescopes to zero exactly when the summands are consecutive differences of a
function. We take this as the definition and build everything on it.

\section{The model}

Fix an integer $n\ge 1$; index patches by the cyclic group $\Zn$. Fix an abelian
group $(A,+,0)$.

\begin{definition}[Local increment data]
A \emph{figure} with $n$ patches and coefficients in $A$ is a function
$t:\Zn\to A$. The value $t_i:=t(i)$ is the increment prescribed on the overlap
from patch $i$ to patch $i+1$ (indices modulo $n$).
\end{definition}

Two interpretations drive the applications: $A=\RR$ gives depth/height increments
(Penrose triangle, Escher staircase); $A=\ZZ/2$ gives orientation bits ($0$
preserve, $1$ reverse; M\"obius band, Klein bottle).

\begin{definition}[Holonomy]
The \emph{holonomy} of a figure $t$ is
$\hol(t):=\sum_{i\in\Zn} t_i \in A.$
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Realizability]
A figure $t$ is \emph{realizable} if there exists a global gauge $h:\Zn\to A$ with
$h(i+1)-h(i)=t_i$ for all $i\in\Zn$.
\end{definition}

In cellular terms, $t$ is a $1$-cochain on a triangulated $S^1$; realizability
says $t$ is a coboundary; the holonomy is the pairing of $t$ with the fundamental
class of the loop.

\section{The master equivalence}

\begin{lemma}[Holonomy of a coboundary vanishes]\label{lem:cob}
For any $h:\Zn\to A$, $\ \hol\big(i\mapsto h(i+1)-h(i)\big)=0.$
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Since $i\mapsto i+1$ is a bijection of $\Zn$, $\sum_i h(i+1)=\sum_i h(i)$, so
$\sum_i\big(h(i+1)-h(i)\big)=0$. This is the discrete Fundamental Theorem of
Calculus on the cycle.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Forward direction]\label{prop:fwd}
If $t$ is realizable then $\hol(t)=0$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
If $t_i=h(i+1)-h(i)$, then $\hol(t)=0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:cob}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Reverse direction]\label{prop:rev}
If $\hol(t)=0$ then $t$ is realizable.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Define the partial-sum gauge $h(i):=\sum_{j=0}^{\val(i)-1} t(j)$, where
$\val(i)\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ is the canonical representative. For $\val(i)+1<n$,
the representative of $i+1$ is $\val(i)+1$ and
$h(i+1)-h(i)=t(\val(i))=t_i$. For the wrap-around step $\val(i)=n-1$, $i+1=0$, we
have $h(i+1)=h(0)=0$ and $h(i)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-2}t(j)$; the hypothesis
$\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}t(j)=0$ gives $\sum_{j=0}^{n-2}t(j)=-t(n-1)$, so
$h(i+1)-h(i)=t(n-1)=t_i$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Master equivalence]\label{thm:master}
A figure $t:\Zn\to A$ is realizable if and only if $\hol(t)=0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Combine Propositions~\ref{prop:fwd} and~\ref{prop:rev}.
\end{proof}

\section{The holonomy is a cohomology class}

\begin{proposition}[Gauge invariance]\label{prop:gauge}
For any figure $t$ and any $c:\Zn\to A$,
$\ \hol\big(i\mapsto t_i+(c(i+1)-c(i))\big)=\hol(t).$
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
By additivity and Lemma~\ref{lem:cob}, the added coboundary contributes $0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Additivity]\label{prop:add}
$\hol(t+s)=\hol(t)+\hol(s)$.
\end{proposition}

Thus $\hol$ is a homomorphism (the \emph{Penrose class map}) with kernel exactly
the realizable figures, well defined on $H^1=(\text{cochains})/(\text{coboundaries})$.

\section{Impossibility of the classical figures ($A=\RR$)}

\begin{theorem}[Penrose triangle]\label{thm:penrose}
The figure with $n=3$ and $t_0=t_1=t_2=1$ is not realizable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\hol(t)=1+1+1=3\ne 0$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:master}. Equivalently, a gauge
would force $0=(h_1-h_0)+(h_2-h_1)+(h_0-h_2)=3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Escher staircase]\label{thm:escher}
If $t_i>0$ for all $i$, then $t$ is not realizable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A sum of strictly positive reals over the nonempty set $\Zn$ is positive, so
$\hol(t)>0\ne 0$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:master}.
\end{proof}

\section{Non-orientable surfaces ($A=\ZZ/2$)}

Let coefficients be $\ZZ/2=\{0,1\}$ with $1+1=0$. The holonomy counts orientation
flips modulo two; a gauge is a global orientation.

\begin{theorem}[Odd holonomy forbids orientation]\label{thm:klein}
If $\hol(s)=1$ in $\ZZ/2$ then $s$ is not realizable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Realizability would force $\hol(s)=0$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:master}, contradicting
$\hol(s)=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[M\"obius band]\label{thm:mobius}
The single-patch figure $n=1$, $t_0=1\in\ZZ/2$ is not realizable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Its holonomy is $1$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:klein}.
\end{proof}

The Klein bottle is the closed one-sided gluing; Theorem~\ref{thm:klein} is
exactly the statement that it carries no global orientation. The Penrose triangle
(real depth) and Klein bottle (mod-two orientation) are one theorem with
different coefficient groups.

\section{The impossibility class is a complete invariant}

\begin{theorem}[Completeness]\label{thm:complete}
For $A=\RR$, a figure $t$ is impossible iff $\hol(t)\ne 0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Negate Theorem~\ref{thm:master}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Surjectivity, $H^1\cong\RR$]\label{thm:surj}
For every $r\in\RR$ there is a figure with $\hol(t)=r$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Take $t_0=r$ and $t_i=0$ for $i\ne 0$.
\end{proof}

Combining Propositions~\ref{prop:gauge}--\ref{prop:add} with
Theorems~\ref{thm:complete}--\ref{thm:surj}, the Penrose class map is a surjective
homomorphism with kernel the realizable figures, so $H^1\cong\RR$: impossibility
is a continuous real-valued measurement.

\section{Impossibility is global, not local}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform yet impossible]\label{thm:unif}
The Penrose triangle has uniform data ($t_i=1$ for all $i$) yet is impossible.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Uniformity is immediate; impossibility is Theorem~\ref{thm:penrose}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Non-uniform yet realizable]\label{thm:nonunif}
The figure $n=3$, $t_0=1,\ t_1=2,\ t_2=-3$ (pairwise distinct) is realizable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\hol(t)=1+2-3=0$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:master}.
\end{proof}

Thus no function of the multiset of local increments determines realizability;
only the ordered sum---the holonomy---does. Impossibility is irreducibly global.

\section{The multiplicative model: developable surfaces}

Fix a commutative group $(G,\cdot,1)$ (Penrose used $\RR_{>0}$ under
multiplication).

\begin{definition}
A \emph{multiplicative figure} is $t:\Zn\to G$ with monodromy
$\mon(t):=\prod_{i\in\Zn}t_i$. It is realizable (developable) if there is a gauge
$h:\Zn\to G$ with $h(i+1)\,h(i)^{-1}=t_i$ for all $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Classification of developable figures]\label{thm:mmaster}
A multiplicative figure is realizable (developable) iff $\mon(t)=1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:master} with $+,0$ replaced by $\cdot,1$: a coboundary
telescopes to $\mon=1$; conversely the partial-product gauge
$h(i)=\prod_{j<\val(i)}t(j)$ realizes $t$, the wrap-around closing precisely when
$\mon(t)=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Monodromy homomorphism]\label{prop:mhom}
$\mon:(\Zn\to G)\to G$ is a surjective group homomorphism whose kernel is exactly
the developable figures; hence $H^1\cong G$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Penrose scaling triangle]\label{thm:mscale}
If every beam of a three-overlap figure scales by the same $g$ with $g^3\ne 1$,
then $\mon=g^3\ne 1$ and the figure is not developable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Contrarian disproof]\label{thm:mcontra}
The conjecture ``if every overlap genuinely rescales ($t_i\ne 1$) then the figure
is impossible'' is false: for $g\ne 1$, the figure $t_0=g,\ t_1=g^{-1}$ has both
factors nontrivial yet is developable, since $\mon(t)=g\,g^{-1}=1$.
\end{theorem}

This project formalizes the mathematical core of impossible figures (Penrose
triangle, Escher staircase) as a cohomological obstruction, following R. Penrose's
insight that impossibility is a *global* holonomy class, not a local defect. Two
self-contained developments were produced and fully proved:

* Additive model over an arbitrary abelian group A. Realizability <=> vanishing
  holonomy; the Penrose triangle and Escher staircase are impossible; orientation
  cocycles in Z/2 give the Moebius/Klein non-orientability; the holonomy is a
  complete R-valued invariant; and a contrarian pair shows impossibility is global
  not local.
* Multiplicative model over an arbitrary commutative group G (Penrose's original
  scaling-ambiguity group). Developability <=> trivial monodromy; monodromy
  packaged as a group homomorphism whose kernel is exactly the developable
  figures; a scaling Penrose triangle is non-developable; and a contrarian
  disproof of "all local factors nontrivial => impossible".

## What was proved vs. disproved (contrarian mission)

Proved.
- The master equivalence (existence of a global gauge <=> trivial class) in both
  additive and multiplicative forms.
- Concrete impossibility results: the Penrose triangle, the closed
  everywhere-ascending staircase, the Klein bottle / Moebius band
  non-orientability, and the non-developability of a scaling Penrose triangle.
- The class is a well-defined, surjective, complete invariant (H^1 = A).

Disproved (bold conjectures refuted by explicit counterexample).
- "Uniform local data is always realizable" — FALSE (the Penrose triangle is
  uniform yet impossible).
- "Non-uniform local data is always impossible" — FALSE (increments 1, 2, -3 are
  pairwise distinct yet realizable).
- "If every overlap genuinely rescales the figure then it is impossible" — FALSE
  (a scale-by-g then scale-by-g^{-1} pair is developable with both factors
  nontrivial).

## Directions not yet formalized

1. True manifold statements. The framing ("every non-orientable 3-manifold
   contains an embedded Penrose triangle as a smoothly immersed surface") requires
   smooth-manifold and singular/de Rham cohomology machinery. The natural bridge
   is: our holonomy is the pairing of a Z/n cellular 1-cocycle with the
   fundamental class of the loop; formalizing it as an element of H^1(S^1; A) and
   relating non-orientability to w_1 != 0 (first Stiefel–Whitney class) is the
   next milestone.

2. Higher figures / branched covers. Replace the single loop by a general finite
   CW-complex; impossibility becomes non-vanishing of a class in H^1(X; A). The
   Penrose triangle becomes one case among richer branched configurations.

3. Continuous and smooth models. Passing from the discrete cycle Z/n to the
   circle S^1 recovers the de Rham picture, where the holonomy is the integral of

The Topology of Impossible Objects: Escher Stairs and Klein Bottles
===================================================================

Numerical demonstrations of the holonomy theory of impossible figures.

A cyclic figure with ``n`` overlapping patches carries local reconciliation
data ``t[0], ..., t[n-1]`` valued in an abelian group.  The figure is
*realizable* (buildable as an honest object) if and only if its **holonomy**
-- the total increment accumulated once around the loop -- is the identity.

    * Additive model  (group = the reals):     holonomy = sum(t),   identity = 0
    * Orientation     (group = Z/2):            holonomy = sum(t) % 2, identity = 0
    * Multiplicative  (group = positive reals): monodromy = prod(t), identity = 1

This script verifies:
    - the Penrose triangle is impossible (holonomy = 3);
    - a closed everywhere-ascending staircase is impossible;
    - a Moebius / Klein gluing (odd number of flips) has no global orientation;
    - impossibility is GLOBAL, not local (uniform-impossible vs distinct-realizable);
    - the reconstructed gauge really induces the local data when holonomy vanishes;
    - the multiplicative (developable-surface) model and its contrarian example.

Self-contained: standard library only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, Optional, Callable, TypeVar

T = TypeVar("T")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Additive model (coefficients in the reals)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def holonomy(t: List[float]) -> float:
    """Total additive increment accumulated once around the cyclic figure."""
    return sum(t)


def is_realizable(t: List[float], tol: float = 1e-12) -> bool:
    """A figure is realizable iff its holonomy vanishes."""
    return abs(holonomy(t)) <= tol


def reconstruct_gauge(t: List[float]) -> Optional[List[float]]:
    """
    Return an explicit global height field h with h[i+1] - h[i] = t[i]
    (indices modulo n), or None if the figure is impossible.

    The gauge is the vector of partial sums: h[i] = t[0] + ... + t[i-1].
    """
    if not is_realizable(t):
        return None
    n = len(t)
    h = [0.0] * n
    running = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        h[i] = running
        running += t[i]
    return h


def verify_gauge(t: List[float], h: List[float], tol: float = 1e-9) -> bool:
    """Check that h[i+1] - h[i] = t[i] cyclically."""
    n = len(t)
    return all(abs((h[(i + 1) % n] - h[i]) - t[i]) <= tol for i in range(n))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Orientation model (coefficients in Z/2)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def holonomy_z2(flips: List[int]) -> int:
    """Total orientation flip around the loop, modulo 2."""
    return sum(f % 2 for f in flips) % 2


def is_orientable(flips: List[int]) -> bool:
    """A closed band is orientable iff its Z/2 holonomy is 0 (even flips)."""
    return holonomy_z2(flips) == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Multiplicative model (coefficients in the positive reals -> developable)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def monodromy(t: List[float]) -> float:
    """Total multiplicative scaling accumulated once around the figure."""
    prod = 1.0
    for x in t:
        prod *= x
    return prod


def is_developable(t: List[float], tol: float = 1e-12) -> bool:
    """A scaling figure is developable iff its monodromy equals 1."""
    return abs(monodromy(t) - 1.0) <= tol


def reconstruct_scale_gauge(t: List[float]) -> Optional[List[float]]:
    """Partial-product gauge h with h[i+1] / h[i] = t[i], or None if impossible."""
    if not is_developable(t):
        return None
    n = len(t)
    h = [1.0] * n
    running = 1.0
    for i in range(n):
        h[i] = running
        running *= t[i]
    return h


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_penrose_triangle() -> None:
    print("=" * 68)
    print("Penrose triangle: three beams, each receding by one unit")
    print("=" * 68)
    t = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
    print(f"  local increments t = {t}")
    print(f"  holonomy          = {holonomy(t)}")
    print(f"  realizable?       = {is_realizable(t)}   (impossible: holonomy = 3)")
    print()


def demo_escher_staircase() -> None:
    print("=" * 68)
    print("Escher staircase: a closed flight where every step ascends")
    print("=" * 68)
    for t in ([1.0, 2.0, 1.5, 0.5], [0.3] * 6):
        print(f"  ascending steps t = {t}")
        print(f"  holonomy          = {holonomy(t):.4f} > 0  ->  impossible")
    print()


def demo_global_not_local() -> None:
    print("=" * 68)
    print("Impossibility is GLOBAL, not local")
    print("=" * 68)
    uniform = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
    distinct = [1.0, 2.0, -3.0]
    print(f"  uniform data  t = {uniform}  (all equal) ->",
          "IMPOSSIBLE" if not is_realizable(uniform) else "realizable",
          f"(holonomy {holonomy(uniform)})")
    print(f"  distinct data t = {distinct} (all differ) ->",
          "impossible" if not is_realizable(distinct) else "REALIZABLE",
          f"(holonomy {holonomy(distinct)})")
    h = reconstruct_gauge(distinct)
    assert h is not None and verify_gauge(distinct, h)
    print(f"  reconstructed height field h = {h}  (verified: h[i+1]-h[i] = t[i])")
    print()


def demo_klein_mobius() -> None:
    print("=" * 68)
    print("Moebius band / Klein bottle: orientation flips modulo 2")
    print("=" * 68)
    mobius = [1]                # one self-gluing with a flip
    cylinder = [1, 1]           # two flips cancel
    klein = [1, 0, 1, 1]        # odd number of flips
    for name, flips in [("Moebius band", mobius),
                        ("plain cylinder", cylinder),
                        ("Klein loop", klein)]:
        ok = is_orientable(flips)
        print(f"  {name:16s} flips={flips!s:14s} holonomy={holonomy_z2(flips)} "
              f"-> {'orientable' if ok else 'NON-orientable'}")
    print()


def demo_developable() -> None:
    print("=" * 68)
    print("Multiplicative model: developable (flat) surfaces")

    g = 1.5

    print(f"  scaling triangle t = {scaling_triangle}  monodromy = {monodromy(scaling_triangle):.4f}"

    print(f"  cancelling pair  t = {cancelling}  monodromy = {monodromy(cancelling):.4f}"
          f"  -> {'DEVELOPABLE' if is_developable(cancelling) else 'not developable'}")
    print("    (contrarian: both factors != 1, yet the figure is developable)")
    h = reconstruct_scale_gauge(cancelling)
    print(f"    reconstructed scale gauge h = {h}")
    print()


def demo_surjectivity() -> None:
    print("=" * 68)
    print("Impossibility is a complete, real-valued invariant (H^1 = R)")
    print("=" * 68)

              f"  ({'realizable' if is_realizable(t) else 'impossible'})")
    print()


def main() -> None:

    demo_escher_staircase()
    demo_global_not_local()
    demo_klein_mobius()
    demo_developable()
    demo_surjectivity()
    print("All demonstrations completed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
